excluded by rat.  On subsequent builds it does exist, so it is

title: RE: why did Kafka choose pull instead of push for a consumer ?
snippet:
Kafka writes each message but the OS is writing those to in memory disk cache.  Kafka periodically calls fsync() to tell the OS to force the disk cache to actual disk.  Kafka gets high availability by replicating messages to other brokers so that the messages are in-memory on several machines at once.  If all the replicas fail around the same time you could lose data.

-Dave
